# `silk/time/plain_date_time`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Dates with a time of day and no time zone: the [`PlainDateTime`](#PlainDateTime) type.

## When to use

Use [`PlainDateTime`](#PlainDateTime) for a wall-clock reading that is not tied to a place, such as "the
meeting is on 2026-11-19 at 17:30" before the place is known, or a timestamp in a file that
states no offset. It is not a point in time. For a point in time, use `silk.time.instant`, and
convert with `Instant.toOffset` and `Instant.fromLocal`.

## Details

A `PlainDateTime` is a `PlainDate` and a `PlainTime`. The range is
`-271821-04-19T00:00:00.000000001` to `+275760-09-13T23:59:59.999999999`, the range of
ECMAScript Temporal.

## `PlainDateTime`

```silk
pub struct PlainDateTime
```

A calendar date and a time of day in the ISO 8601 calendar, with no time zone.

### Details

The range is `-271821-04-19T00:00:00.000000001` to `+275760-09-13T23:59:59.999999999`. `==`,
`!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare the date first and then the time. `Display` writes
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, with a fraction when the nanosecond part is not zero.

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make(date: PlainDate, time: PlainTime) -> PlainDateTime
```

Returns `time` on the day `date`.

#### Gotchas

Midnight on the first date of the range, `-271821-04-19`, is outside the range and traps.
[`PlainDateTime.checkedMake`](#PlainDateTime.impl.checkedMake) returns `None` instead.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.toEpochSeconds"></a>

### Method `toEpochSeconds`

```silk
pub fn toEpochSeconds(self: Self) -> i64
```

Returns the whole seconds from `1970-01-01T00:00:00` to this date and time, rounded toward
negative infinity, with every day counted as 86,400 seconds.

#### Details

When the value is a reading in UTC, the result is its Unix time. The rest of the value is
the nanosecond part of [`PlainDateTime.time`](#PlainDateTime.impl.time).

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.fromEpochSeconds"></a>

### Associated function `fromEpochSeconds`

```silk
pub fn fromEpochSeconds(seconds: i64, nanosecond: u32) -> Option<PlainDateTime>
```

Returns the date and time that is `seconds` seconds plus `nanosecond` nanoseconds after
`1970-01-01T00:00:00`, with every day counted as 86,400 seconds, or `None` when it is outside
the range or `nanosecond` is above 999,999,999.

#### Details

`seconds` can be negative; the nanosecond part always counts forward. With a Unix time, the
result is the reading in UTC.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.checkedAdd"></a>

### Method `checkedAdd`

```silk
pub fn checkedAdd(self: Self, span: Duration) -> Option<PlainDateTime>
```

Returns the date and time `span` later, or earlier for a negative span, or `None` when it is
outside the range.

#### Details

Every day counts as 24 hours. A `PlainDateTime` has no time zone, so the result does not
account for a daylight saving change.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.add"></a>

### Method `add`

```silk
pub fn add(self: Self, span: Duration) -> PlainDateTime
```

Returns the date and time `span` later, or earlier for a negative span. Every day counts as
24 hours.

#### Gotchas

A result outside the range traps. [`PlainDateTime.checkedAdd`](#PlainDateTime.impl.checkedAdd) returns `None` instead.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.until"></a>

### Method `until`

```silk
pub fn until(self: Self, other: PlainDateTime) -> Duration
```

Returns the exact span from this date and time to `other`, with every day counted as 24
hours. It is negative when `other` is earlier.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.checkedAddPeriod"></a>

### Method `checkedAddPeriod`

```silk
pub fn checkedAddPeriod(self: Self, period: Period, overflow: Overflow) -> Option<PlainDateTime>
```

Returns the date and time that `period` leads to, or `None` when it is outside the range,
or when `overflow` is `Reject` and the day does not exist in the month reached.

#### Details

The time part of the period is added to the time of day, and the whole days that it
crosses go to the days of the period. Then the date moves as in
`PlainDate.checkedAddPeriod`: years and months first, with the day held to the month
reached, and then weeks and days. Every day counts as 24 hours.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.addPeriod"></a>

### Method `addPeriod`

```silk
pub fn addPeriod(self: Self, period: Period) -> PlainDateTime
```

Returns the date and time that `period` leads to, with a day that does not exist in the
month reached replaced by the last day of that month.

#### Gotchas

A result outside the range traps. [`PlainDateTime.checkedAddPeriod`](#PlainDateTime.impl.checkedAddPeriod) returns `None`
instead.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.periodUntil"></a>

### Method `periodUntil`

```silk
pub fn periodUntil(self: Self, other: PlainDateTime, largest: DateUnit) -> Period
```

Returns the calendar span from this date and time to `other`: years, months, weeks, or
days as `largest` says, and the time that is left, which is less than 24 hours. It is
negative when `other` is earlier.

#### Details

The date parts are counted as in `PlainDate.periodUntil`, up to the last whole day before
`other`. Every day counts as 24 hours. For the exact span in hours and smaller units, use
[`PlainDateTime.until`](#PlainDateTime.impl.until).

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<PlainDateTime, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a date and time from ISO 8601 text such as `2026-11-19T17:36:22.5`.

#### Details

The text is a date, `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYYMMDD`, then optionally `T`, `t`, or a space and a
time: `HH`, `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, `HHMM`, or `HHMMSS`, with an optional fraction of one to
nine digits. A text without a time reads as midnight. Second `60` reads as `59`. A numeric
UTC offset and bracketed annotations can follow, as in
`2026-11-19T17:36:22+01:00[Europe/Rome]`. They are checked and then ignored.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as month 13 or hour 24,
  or the value is outside the range.
- `TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed` if the text has the UTC designator `Z`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.

Reads a date and time from the bytes of ISO 8601 text such as `2026-11-19T17:36:22.5`.

#### Details

The text is a date, `YYYY-MM-DD` or `YYYYMMDD`, then optionally `T`, `t`, or a space and a
time: `HH`, `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, `HHMM`, or `HHMMSS`, with an optional fraction of one to
nine digits. A text without a time reads as midnight. Second `60` reads as `59`. A numeric
UTC offset and bracketed annotations can follow. They are checked and then ignored.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as month 13 or hour 24,
  or the value is outside the range.
- `TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed` if the text has the UTC designator `Z`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.

<a id="PlainDateTime.impl.write"></a>

### Method `write`

```silk
pub fn write(self: Self, output: &mut [u8], at: usize) -> usize
```

Writes the date and time as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` at `output[at]`, with a fraction when the
nanosecond part is not zero, and returns the offset after it. The text is at most 32 bytes.
